title: Zariski square-zero ring-sheaf extensions with quasi-coherent kernel are schemes
statement: Let $f:X\to B$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. On the Zariski space $|X|$ let $0\to G\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal E\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal O_X\to0$ be an exact sequence of underlying additive sheaves, where $\mathcal E$ is a sheaf of commutative unital $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$-algebras, $p$ is an algebra map, and $i(G)$ is an ideal of square zero with the prescribed quotient $\mathcal O_X$-module action. Here exactness refers to underlying additive sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $X_{\mathcal E}=(|X|,\mathcal E)$ is a scheme, its quotient map gives a first order thickening $X\hookrightarrow X_{\mathcal E}$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] over $B$, and every first order thickening over $B$ is obtained this way with its actual kernel. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, the map $\mathcal E(U)\to A$ is surjective with kernel $G(U)$ and $(U,\mathcal E|_U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal E(U)$ canonically. Maps of these ring extensions reducing to the identity of $\mathcal O_X$ correspond contravariantly and bijectively to morphisms of the associated thickenings over $B$ restricting to the identity on $X$. The construction and this correspondence commute with open restriction.

source.place: Tag 05YV (lemma-first-order-thickening), statement and affine construction in the proof; morphisms are morphisms of the resulting locally ringed spaces.

proof.text: Taking stalks gives exact square-zero ring extensions $0\to G_x\to\mathcal E_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to0$, by the short-exact-stalkwise criterion. In any surjective ring map with square-zero kernel, an element is a unit exactly when its image is: if $ab=1+k$ with $k^2=0$, then $b(1-k)$ is an inverse to $a$; the converse follows by applying the ring map. Thus the nonunits of $\mathcal E_x$ are exactly the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and form its unique maximal ideal. Consequently $Z=(|X|,\mathcal E)$ is a locally ringed space and $(\mathrm{id}_{|X|},p):X\to Z$ is local on stalks.

source.place: Tag 05YV, opening sentence: the extension is a locally ringed space; unit calculation supplied

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ and put $R=\mathcal E(U)$ and $I=G(U)$. The sequence restricts to a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $U$: local lifts witnessing a sheaf epimorphism remain local lifts on an open subset, and kernels are unchanged by restriction. Affine vanishing gives $H^1(U,G|_U)=0$ in modules, and the Zariski module-to-abelian comparison gives the same vanishing for its underlying abelian sheaf. Apply the right-derived long exact sequence to global sections of the restricted abelian-sheaf sequence. Its initial segment, using $R^0\Gamma=\Gamma$, is $0\to I\to R\to A\to H^1(U,G)=0$. Hence $q:R\to A$ is surjective with kernel $I$. The ideal $I$ has square zero, since its multiplication is computed sectionwise in $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Tag 05YV, affine section extension; Tag 01XB (coherent.tex, lemma-quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero), Tag 03FD (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), and Tags 015B/05TE for the long exact sequence

proof.text: Apply the locally ringed space--affine adjunction to $Z|_U$ and the identity of $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal E)$. It gives a canonical morphism $h:Z|_U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Naturality of the adjunction shows that $h\circ (X|_U\to Z|_U)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}q$ under $X|_U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, because both correspond to $q:R\to A$. The surjection $q$ defines a closed immersion. Every prime of $R$ contains $I$: for $a\in I$ one has $a^2=0$, so primality forces $a$ into the prime. Conversely inverse image under $q$ identifies primes of $A=R/I$ with these primes of $R$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}q$ is surjective and, being a closed immersion, is a homeomorphism. The map $X|_U\to Z|_U$ is the identity on points, so $h$ is a homeomorphism as well.

source.place: Tag 05YV, canonical morphism and the displayed square; Tag 01I1 (schemes.tex, lemma-morphism-into-affine). The identity of R is used, correcting the displayed proof text B-to-Gamma typo

proof.text: Let $x\in U$, let $\mathfrak m\subset A$ be its prime, and set $\mathfrak p=q^{-1}(\mathfrak m)\subset R$. Localize the section sequence of step 2 at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$. Localization preserves short exact sequences, so its row is $0\to I_{\mathfrak p}\to R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak m}\to0$. Here the image of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ in $A$ is exactly $A\setminus\mathfrak m$: lift any denominator by surjectivity of $q$. Regard the bottom stalk row from step 1 as $R$-modules using germs. Its vertical comparison with this row sends a fraction to the germ of its numerator times the inverse germ of its denominator. For the kernel this is the prescribed quotient action; therefore $I_{\mathfrak p}\to G_x$ is the localization isomorphism from the affine-module germ theorem, applied to the quasi-coherent $G|_U$. For the quotient, $A_{\mathfrak m}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the affine-module germ theorem applied to $\mathcal O_X|_U$ (represented by the module $A$). Its quasi-coherence follows directly from the affine-local definition. The middle map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal E_x$ is $h_x^\sharp$ under the spectrum stalk formula, because the adjunction map is the identity on global sections. All squares commute on fractions by the formulas just given. The short five lemma on additive groups makes this middle ring map an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05YV, displayed short exact stalk diagram and its comparison; Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), localization exactness, and the short five lemma

proof.text: Over the homeomorphism $h$, the ring-sheaf map $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\to h_*(\mathcal E|_U)$ has bijective stalks by step 4; inverse image of open sets under a homeomorphism identifies the two neighbourhood systems, hence identifies the pushforward stalk with $\mathcal E_x$. The sheaf-of-sets stalk criterion makes the map bijective on every open. Its sectionwise inverses preserve ring operations and restrictions, since the original maps do. They therefore give an inverse morphism of ringed spaces, and are local on stalks because they are ring isomorphisms. Thus $h$ is canonically an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces. Every point of $Z$ lies in such a $U$, so $Z$ is a scheme by the definition. This proves both claimed affine assertions for every affine open, not just one chosen cover. The quotient morphism $X\to Z$ is a closed immersion (identity on points and a surjective structure-sheaf map) and its defining ideal is $i(G)$ with square zero. It is therefore a first order thickening.

source.place: Tag 05YV, conclusion from the stalk comparison; Sheaves Tag 007T (lemma-points-exactness), part (3)

proof.text: The given $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$-algebra structure is, by the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction, a map $\mathcal O_B\to f_*\mathcal E$, hence a morphism of ringed spaces $Z\to B$ with point map $|f|$. This map is local: if the image of $b\in\mathcal O_{B,f(x)}$ in $\mathcal E_x$ is a unit, its image in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a unit, so $b$ is a unit by locality of $f$; all ring maps preserve units. The structure map is thus a scheme morphism. Since $p$ is an algebra map, its composite with $X\to Z$ is exactly $f$, on both points and ring maps. This equips the first order thickening with the asserted structure over $B$.

source.place: Tag 05YV, base algebra structure and conclusion over S; locality is checked using the unit calculation of step 1

proof.text: Conversely let $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be any first order thickening over $B$. It is a homeomorphism by the definition of a finite order thickening, so identify its point space with $|X|$. Let $J=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_X)$ be its actual ideal sheaf. The closed-immersion ideal theorem says that $J$ is quasi-coherent over $\mathcal O_Y$; the first order hypothesis says $J^2=0$. In the closed-immersion annihilated-module theorem, take the quasi-coherent module to be $J$ itself: its annihilation hypothesis is exactly $J^2=0$. The theorem gives a quasi-coherent $j^*J$ on $X$ and an isomorphism $J\to j_*j^*J$. Since $j$ is the identity after identifying spaces, this identifies the actual underlying sheaf $J$ with a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Its quotient action is the prescribed one: any two lifts of a local scalar differ by a section of $J$, whose product with $J$ is zero. The structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Y$, its actual kernel and quotient, and its map from $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$ are consequently extension data of the kind assumed. Applying the construction recovers $Y$ with these data, since it uses exactly this space and sheaf.

source.place: Tag 05YV, moreover clause; Tag 01QY (morphisms.tex, lemma-i-star-equivalence) supplies quasi-coherence with the quotient action

proof.text: For two extension sheaves $\mathcal E_1,\mathcal E_2$, a map $\alpha:\mathcal E_2\to\mathcal E_1$ of the base algebras commuting with their quotient maps gives a ringed-space morphism $(|X|,\mathcal E_1)\to(|X|,\mathcal E_2)$ with identity point map. It is local: in either stalk an element is a unit precisely when its image in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a unit by step 1, and the reduction of $\alpha$ is the identity. It is over $B$ by the algebra condition and restricts to $\mathrm{id}_X$ by the quotient condition. Conversely any such scheme morphism has identity point map, because both thickening inclusions identify their spaces with $|X|$. Its structure-sheaf map is therefore exactly such an $\alpha$. These operations are inverse on the point maps and on every component of the sheaf maps. The composition formula for ringed-space morphisms gives the stated contravariance.

source.place: Tag 05YV, morphism enhancement from the definition of locally ringed space morphisms; unit calculation of step 1

proof.text: For an open subset $V\subseteq |X|$, restriction of the construction is literally $(V,\mathcal E|_V)$ and the inclusion is the restricted quotient map. The restricted kernel is $G|_V$, still quasi-coherent by its affine-local definition. The maps correspondence of step 8 sends $\alpha$ to its component sheaf map and therefore sends its restriction to $\alpha|_V$. The canonical affine identifications also respect further open restrictions: the adjunction morphism of step 3 is natural, and the comparisons in step 4 use only germs and inverses of denominators, both of which commute with restriction. No affine-intersection assumption is needed; restrictions may be checked on affine neighbourhoods inside any intersection. This proves all claimed restriction compatibilities.

source.place: Tag 05YV, construction on arbitrary affine opens; naturality and restriction enhancement
